summary: Re-review the 9 hardening fixes (commit ed07d9ba): correctness + regression + new-issue, firsthand

result.dimension: FIX5 (CSRF intent) + FIX7 (CORS preflight) in src-tauri/src/web_api/middleware/auth.rs (+ routes.rs ordering)
result.summary: FIX7 (OPTIONS+Origin passthrough) and FIX5 (cross-site intent check) are both correct and regression-free for the deployed IPv4/Tailscale single-operator path. I verified firsthand against tower-http 0.5.2 source that an OPTIONS request can NEVER reach a mutation handler: CorsService::call short-circuits on ANY Method::OPTIONS (mod.rs:630) without invoking the inner service, and the mutation routes register only post()/put() (no options()). So a state-changing op cannot be smuggled as OPTIONS to dodge FIX5. FIX5's logic (Sec-Fetch-Site none/same-origin allow; same-site/cross-site/null reject; Origin<->Host fallback; absent-Origin allow for CLI) is sound, never over-allows a cross-site host, and does not break the same-origin SPA. All 7 new auth unit tests compile and pass under the real web-server build. One genuine NEW bug: the Host-header port-stripping h.split(':').next() corrupts bracketed IPv6 literals, producing a false-DENY (403) for legitimate same-origin IPv6 requests lacking Sec-Fetch-Site — security-direction-safe (over-blocks, never over-allows) and inert on the deployed IPv4 host, hence low severity.

findings.title: FIX7 OPTIONS+Origin passthrough cannot smuggle a mutation: tower-http short-circuits ALL OPTIONS before the handler
findings.evidence: auth.rs:190 `if req.method() == Method::OPTIONS && req.headers().contains_key(header::ORIGIN) { return next.run(req).await; }` lets OPTIONS bypass FIX5+auth. I verified firsthand that this is safe: tower-http-0.5.2/src/cors/mod.rs:630 `if parts.method == Method::OPTIONS {` returns `Kind::PreflightCall { headers }` UNCONDITIONALLY (it does NOT require Access-Control-Request-Method) and NEVER calls `self.inner.call(req)` — the route handler is not invoked. The mutation routes register only POST/PUT (proxy.rs:71 `post(start_proxy_server)`, :78 `put(set_proxy_takeover_for_app)`), no `.options()`, so axum would 405 OPTIONS even if CorsLayer didn't intercept. The CorsLayer is the innermost layer on api_router (routes.rs:67 `.layer(mw::cors::layer())`), and the outer require_auth `next.run(req)` descends into it.
findings.impact: No state-changing operation can ride an OPTIONS request. An unauthenticated OPTIONS reaches only the CorsLayer's static preflight response.
findings.recommendation: No change. Correct as implemented and tested (is_state_changing_classifies_methods asserts OPTIONS is not state-changing).

findings.title: FIX7 leaks nothing beyond static CORS headers: default empty allow-list emits no Access-Control-Allow-Origin
findings.evidence: cors.rs sets no `allow_origin` unless CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS is present; tower-http-0.5.2/src/cors/allow_origin.rs:152 `impl Default for OriginInner { fn default() -> Self { Self::List(Vec::new()) } }` and to_header (allow_origin.rs:100) `OriginInner::List(l) => origin.filter(|o| l.contains(o))?.clone()` returns None for an empty list. So the unauth OPTIONS preflight response carries NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin → the browser blocks the subsequent cross-origin actual request. CorsLayer answers 200 for OPTIONS uniformly regardless of whether the /api path exists (it short-circuits before routing), so no endpoint-existence oracle is introduced.
findings.impact: An unauth attacker probing via OPTIONS+Origin learns only the constant allow-methods/allow-headers values — no app data, no auth state, no route enumeration.
findings.recommendation: No change. The default same-origin-only posture neutralizes the passthrough.

findings.title: FIX5 cross-site intent logic is correct: none/same-origin allow is CSRF-safe, same-site/cross-site/null rejected, never over-allows a foreign host
findings.evidence: auth.rs:140 `"same-origin" | "none" => Ok(())` — `none` is only emitted for user-initiated top-level navigation (address bar/bookmark), which an attacker page cannot forge; a cross-origin form-POST or fetch yields `cross-site` (auth.rs:142 `_ => Err(forbidden(...))`), not `none`. `same-site` is also rejected (correct: a sibling subdomain is untrusted; moot for a raw-IP host with no subdomains). The Origin<->Host fallback uses url::Url::host_str() for Origin (auth.rs:156-158, correctly strips port/brackets) and compares against the Host host portion (auth.rs:159-163); origin_host can never be a truncated artifact like `"["`, so a cross-site host can never wrongly compare-equal — the only failure mode is over-blocking, never over-allowing. `null` Origin → 403 (auth.rs:153-155). Absent Origin → allow (auth.rs:149-151), intended for CLI/server-to-server where Basic auth is the control.
findings.impact: Forged cross-site state-changing POSTs with browser-cached Basic creds are rejected with 403 before auth runs; the same-origin SPA (always Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin) and CLI clients are unaffected.
findings.recommendation: No change. Verified by passing tests cross_site_origin_post_is_rejected, cross_site_fetch_metadata_post_is_rejected, opaque_null_origin_post_is_rejected, same_origin_post_passes_intent_check.

findings.title: FIX5 correctly scopes to mutating verbs and runs before auth; no state-changing GET route exists to dodge the check
findings.evidence: auth.rs:114-118 `is_state_changing` matches only POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; GET/HEAD/OPTIONS skip FIX5 (auth.rs:196). I grepped all handler routers for state-changing ops registered on get() and found only read-only handlers (get_*, check_skill_updates, get_update_info) — no start/stop/set/update/delete is wired to GET, so skipping GET is safe. Order in require_auth is public-check (auth.rs:183) -> OPTIONS passthrough (190) -> FIX5 for mutations (196) -> Basic auth (202). Running FIX5 before auth means a forged cross-site POST is 403'd even with valid cached creds. The 403-vs-401 ordering reveals only 'this is a mutating /api path with a bad cross-site intent' to an attacker who already controls a cross-site page; it leaks no secret and no per-route existence (all mutating /api/* paths behave identically).
findings.impact: No mutation can ride a GET to bypass the intent check; the pre-auth placement is the intended hardening.
findings.recommendation: No change.

findings.title: FIX5 IPv6 Host port-stripping corrupts bracketed literals, causing a false-DENY (403) for genuine same-origin IPv6 requests
findings.evidence: auth.rs:163 strips the Host port via `h.split(':').next().unwrap_or(h)`. For a bracketed IPv6 Host this splits on the FIRST colon inside the address: Host `[::1]:3010` -> request_host `"["`; Host `[2001:db8::1]:8080` -> `"[2001"`. Meanwhile the Origin side uses url::Url::host_str() (auth.rs:156-158), which for `http://[::1]:3010` returns `"::1"` (brackets+port stripped). So origin_host `"::1"` != request_host `"["` -> the match arm at auth.rs:166 `(Some(o), Some(h)) if o == h` fails -> 403 on a legitimate same-origin IPv6 request. This path is only reached when Sec-Fetch-Site is absent (auth.rs:133 returns early when present), i.e. an older/non-Chromium browser or a tool that sends Origin but not fetch-metadata, AND the host is an IPv6 literal.
findings.impact: Availability/correctness only — it over-blocks; it never over-allows (origin_host from url can never equal a truncated `"["`-style artifact, so a cross-site host cannot be smuggled). Inert on the deployed target http://100.75.197.120:3010/ (IPv4) and inert for modern browsers (which always send Sec-Fetch-Site). Bites only an IPv6 deployment (e.g. [::1] loopback / Tailscale IPv6) reached by a fetch-metadata-less client.
findings.recommendation: Strip the Host port with IPv6-aware parsing instead of split(':').next(): if the value starts with '[', take up to the closing ']' (and lowercase the inner literal) before comparing; or parse via `format!("http://{host}").parse::<url::Url>()` and use host_str() symmetrically with the Origin side. Add a test for Host `[::1]:3010` + Origin `http://[::1]:3010` expecting Ok.

result.dimension: FIX1 (usage SSRF + guard_outbound_url SSOT) + FIX2 (get_guarded) + FIX8 (ip_guard exotic ranges)
result.summary: Firsthand-verified FIX1/FIX2/FIX8 in the ed07d9ba delta. All three are correct and regression-free against their stated goals; all 12 relevant unit tests (7 ip_guard, 2 usage_script web-guard, 3 common delegation) pass under BOTH the desktop (`cargo test`) and the real web build (`--example server --features web-server`). The FIX8 `to_ipv4()` false-positive concern is empirically unfounded: a probe confirms `to_ipv4()` returns None for every real public IPv6 (2606:4700:4700::1111, 2001:4860:4860::8888, 2a00:1450::, doc 2001:db8::), so no public v6 is wrongly blocked. The FIX1 SSOT move reproduces the old validate_outbound_url logic exactly (identical error strings, early allow-list return, scheme/host/lookup_host paths) and is threaded correctly (web callers pass enforce=true, desktop pass false; guard fires pre-dial; dials via get_guarded for redirect re-check). FIX2 switched all user-URL dials in the 4 services with none missed and none over-switched. One genuine LOW-severity desktop parity change: get_guarded() is not feature-gated, so its redirect policy now aborts internal-IP-literal redirect HOPS for desktop callers of stream_check/speedtest/webdav/s3 too (initial internal dials still work — policy only fires on 3xx). Both features compile clean.

findings.title: FIX8 ip_guard exotic ranges: correct, no public-IPv6 false positives
findings.evidence: is_blocked_ipv6 line 64 `if let Some(v4) = ip.to_ipv4()` then is_blocked_ipv4. Probe (rustc) proves to_ipv4() == None for 2606:4700:4700::1111, 2001:4860:4860::8888, 2a00:1450:4001::1, 2001:db8::1 (all segment[0]!=0) and Some only for ::ffff:x.x.x.x (mapped) / ::w.x.y.z (compat). is_blocked_ip line 112 routes V6 via to_ipv4_mapped() first, so ::ffff:8.8.8.8 -> is_blocked_ipv4(8.8.8.8)=false (allowed). Masks verified: 0.0.0.0/8 `octets[0]==0` (line 37), multicast/240 (38-39), 6to4 `segments[0]==0x2002` (81), Teredo `0x2001 && seg[1]==0` (85 — db8 has seg[1]=0x0db8 so NOT over-blocked), NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 (89-97), ff00::/8 (99). Test allows_normal_public_addresses + blocks_exotic_ipv6_ranges both assert 2606:4700:4700::1111 is allowed and PASS (7/7 green in desktop and web builds).
findings.impact: FIX8 closes the exotic-range gap (0.0.0.0/8, v4 multicast/reserved, ::a.b.c.d compat, 6to4/NAT64/Teredo/v6-multicast) without blocking any legitimate public address. No over-blocking.
findings.recommendation: No action. Note (info-only): NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 and 6to4 2002:: embed PUBLIC v4 yet are blocked as defense-in-depth — intended per threat model; harmless for single-operator dual-stack usage since direct v4/v6 still works.

findings.title: FIX1 guard_outbound_url SSOT move reproduces old validate_outbound_url exactly
findings.evidence: Diff of 072d3d68:common.rs vs ip_guard.rs guard_outbound_url shows identical control flow: scheme http/https-only reject; Host::Ipv4/Ipv6 `!ssrf_host_allowed && is_blocked` reject; Host::Domain early `Ok(())` on allow-list (line 199-201), else lookup_host any-blocked reject. common::validate_outbound_url now maps OutboundUrlError -> ApiError preserving every original message string verbatim ('Invalid URL', 'Unsupported URL scheme ... only http and https are allowed', 'URL ... has no host', 'Failed to resolve host', 'Refusing to reach internal address'). The 3 delegation tests (validate_outbound_url_blocks_internal_ip_literals / allows_public_ip_literals / rejects_non_http_schemes) PASS under the real web build (cargo test --features web-server --example server).
findings.impact: No behavior change for existing callers (subscription/s3/usage/providers/webdav/config handlers still call validate_outbound_url before invoking services). SSOT removes divergence risk between the request guard and the usage guard.
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.title: FIX1 enforce_outbound_guard threading: web=true / desktop=false on every caller, guard fires pre-dial
findings.evidence: send_http_request lines 392-396 guard_outbound_url(&config.url).await before connecting; lines 398-401 pick get_guarded() when enforce else get(). Threaded through execute_usage_script -> execute_and_format_usage_result -> query_usage / query_usage_with_templates / test_usage_script (all gained the bool). WEB callers: providers.rs query_provider_usage passes `true` (line 528), usage.rs test_usage_script passes `true` (line 348). DESKTOP callers: commands/provider.rs queryProviderUsage + testUsageScript pass `false` (lines 144,200). grep confirms ProviderService::query_usage(non-template) has NO external caller, so no web path defaults to false. Test web_guard_rejects_internal_request_url_before_dial PASSES for 169.254.169.254 / 127.0.0.1:9999 / 10.0.0.1 / 100.64.0.1 — the 9999 port would ECONNREFUSED if the guard didn't fire first, proving pre-dial rejection. Redirect re-check via get_guarded() confirmed (http_client.rs guarded_redirect_policy stops internal IP-literal hops).
findings.impact: Custom-template scripts (which bypass HTTPS/same-origin/base_url checks) can no longer reach internal/metadata/CGNAT endpoints from the web runtime; desktop local dials remain unrestricted (behavior unchanged).
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.title: FIX2 get_guarded() swap: all user-URL dials switched, none missed, none over-switched
findings.evidence: git diff shows every `http_client::get()` in the 4 services replaced by `get_guarded()`. Post-fix grep for `http_client::get()` / `client = .*get(` across stream_check.rs, webdav.rs, s3.rs, speedtest.rs returns ZERO hits — no unguarded user-URL dial remains. Each swapped call dials a user-supplied endpoint (S3/MinIO endpoint, WebDAV base_url, provider base_url for stream-check, speedtest URLs), so all are appropriate; no internal/fixed-URL get() was switched unnecessarily.
findings.impact: Web runtime: a validated public endpoint cannot 30x-redirect to an internal IP literal across all four sync/test services.
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.title: FIX2 desktop parity: get_guarded() is not feature-gated, so it now aborts internal-IP-literal redirect hops for DESKTOP callers of the 4 services too
findings.lines: 245-311 (get_guarded / guarded_redirect_policy, no cfg gate); callers: commands/stream_check.rs 38, commands/provider.rs 218 (SpeedtestService), services s3_sync/webdav_sync
findings.evidence: guarded_redirect_policy (lines 293-311) calls is_blocked_ip on each redirect hop and attempt.stop() for internal IP literals; it is plain runtime code with NO `#[cfg(feature)]` gate (grep for cfg in http_client.rs shows none on get_guarded/policy). Desktop commands DO reach these services: commands/stream_check.rs:38 StreamCheckService::check_with_retry, commands/provider.rs:218 SpeedtestService::test_endpoints, plus webdav/s3 via sync services. So a desktop user whose self-hosted internal endpoint issues a 30x redirect to ANOTHER internal IP-literal (e.g. 127.0.0.1/a -> 192.168.x.y/b) now has that redirect aborted, whereas the old get() followed it.
findings.impact: Behavior change vs. prior desktop. LOW because: (1) initial dials to internal IPs still succeed — reqwest only invokes the redirect Policy on 3xx, never on the first request, so self-hosted endpoints reached directly are unaffected; (2) internal-to-internal HTTP redirects are rare for S3/WebDAV/OpenAI-compat APIs. No crash, no data loss — only an aborted redirect surfaced as a request error in the uncommon redirect case.
findings.recommendation: Accept as intentional defense-in-depth (the redirect block is desirable even on desktop), OR if strict desktop parity is required, gate get_guarded() to return get() under #[cfg(not(feature="web-server"))]. Given the single-operator threat model, accepting is reasonable; document the desktop redirect-policy change in the fix note.

result.dimension: FIX3 (log truncation) + FIX4 (F9 atomicity) — src-tauri/src/proxy/handlers.rs, src-tauri/src/services/proxy.rs
result.summary: Verified both fixes firsthand against the 072d3d68→HEAD delta. FIX4 (switch-then-persist reorder in set_auto_failover_enabled) is correct and a net improvement: the DB flag is now written strictly AFTER a successful switch, the disable path is untouched, the provider-switched emit + unconditional refresh_tray still fire on success, and both desktop (commands/failover.rs:89) and web (web_api/handlers/failover.rs:131) reach the same SSOT. FIX3 (compact_error_message at handlers.rs:1056) is char-based/UTF-8-safe, bounds ONLY the request_log DB persist path, and leaves the client-facing response untruncated as claimed. Three failover tests + the FIX3 truncation test all pass under web-server; desktop lib compiles clean. ONE real gap: FIX3's "any other persist path" claim is incomplete — forwarder.rs:911 still persists the full untruncated upstream body (incl. {body:?}) into the provider_health.last_error DB column via record_result→update_provider_health_with_threshold. Separately, the pre-existing empty-queue auto-add (proxy.rs:2370) mutates the queue before the switch, so a failed switch leaves the current provider in the failover queue — pre-existing, not worsened by FIX4, low severity.

findings.title: FIX4 switch-then-persist reorder is correct and a net improvement over the prior persist-then-switch
findings.evidence: New ordering: `config.auto_failover_enabled = enabled;` (2394) then `if enabled { self.switch_proxy_target(app_type, &p1_provider_id).await?; }` (2401-2403) BEFORE `self.db.update_proxy_config_for_app(config).await?` (2405-2408). The `?` on the switch returns Err before the flag is persisted. Compare 072d3d68 where update_proxy_config_for_app ran at line ~2398 BEFORE the switch, so a switch failure left auto_failover_enabled=true persisted while the API returned Err (divergence). switch_proxy_target genuinely can Err: hot_switch_provider_inner returns Err for official providers at proxy.rs:2157-2162 BEFORE any DB mutation. New test enable_auto_failover_does_not_persist_flag_when_switch_fails passes (flag stays false on switch failure).
findings.impact: Eliminates the state divergence (flag=true persisted + API Err) that the prior ordering produced on switch failure. Strictly safer.
findings.recommendation: No action — fix verified correct and regression-free.

findings.title: FIX4 disable path, success emit, and unconditional refresh_tray all preserved across the reorder
findings.evidence: Disable path: `else { String::new() }` (2384-2386) skips the switch (guarded by `if enabled` at 2401), persists the flag (2405-2408), skips the emit (`if enabled` at 2411), and reaches `if let Some(ctx) = self.runtime_ctx().await { ctx.refresh_tray(); }` (2426-2428) unconditionally. No early-return between the success persist and refresh_tray. provider-switched emit (2411-2422) still fires only on the enable-success path. Tests disable_auto_failover_keeps_queue_and_only_flips_flag and enable_auto_failover_on_empty_queue_auto_adds_current_provider both pass; desktop (commands/failover.rs:89) and web (web_api/handlers/failover.rs:131) both call this one SSOT.
findings.impact: Desktop/web parity and tray-refresh-on-both-paths invariant maintained.
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.title: FIX3 truncates ONLY the DB request_log; client-facing response stays untruncated and truncation is UTF-8 safe
findings.evidence: log_forward_error builds `let error_message = compact_error_message(&get_error_message(error), 400);` (1056) and passes it ONLY into `logger.log_error_with_context(...)` (1059-1070) — the request-log DB write. No response is constructed here (client errors are built in codex_proxy_error_json / chat_error_to_response_error elsewhere). compact_error_message uses `normalized.chars().count()` and `normalized.chars().take(max_chars)` (863, 868-870) — char-based, multi-byte safe. 400 chars preserves status code + leading body. Test upstream_error_body_is_truncated_before_db_persistence passes.
findings.impact: Bounds prompt/token/HTML leakage into the request_log DB without degrading the client error contract.
findings.recommendation: No action for this path.

findings.title: FIX3 is incomplete: the full untruncated upstream body still persists into provider_health.last_error DB column via the forwarder failure path
findings.evidence: On a Retryable upstream failure the forwarder calls `self.router.record_result(&provider.id, app_type_str, used_half_open_permit, false, Some(e.to_string()))` (911). For ProxyError::UpstreamError the Display impl is `#[error("上游错误 (状态码 {status}): {body:?}")]` (error.rs:42-43), i.e. e.to_string() embeds the FULL upstream body. record_result → update_provider_health_with_threshold (provider_router.rs:219-227) → UPSERT INTO provider_health(... last_error ...) VALUES(... ?7=error_msg ...) (dao/proxy.rs:611-631; column declared at schema.rs:179). No compact_error_message wrapping anywhere on this path. FIX3's own comment at handlers.rs:1051-1055 implies the request-log was the persist concern, but the FIX claims to address upstream-body leakage broadly while this second DB persist path remains untruncated.
findings.impact: The same prompts/request-fragments/tokens/large-HTML that FIX3 strips from request_log are still written verbatim to provider_health.last_error (one row per provider, last-write-wins, so bounded in count but unbounded in size per entry). Operator-gated single-user threat model keeps this low, but it is a defense-in-depth/privacy gap the fix claimed to close.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the error string at the forwarder record_result call sites (or inside update_provider_health_with_threshold) with compact_error_message(&e.to_string(), 400) so both DB persist paths are bounded consistently.

findings.title: FIX4: empty-queue auto-add mutates the failover queue before the switch, so a failed enable leaves the current (e.g. official) provider stuck in the queue
findings.evidence: When the queue is empty, the current provider is committed to the queue via `self.db.add_to_failover_queue(app_type, &current_id)` (2370-2372) BEFORE the switch at 2401-2403. In the exact failure scenario FIX4's new test exercises (current provider is official → switch_proxy_target Errs at hot_switch_provider_inner proxy.rs:2157), the official provider has ALREADY been persisted into the failover queue when the function returns Err. The new test asserts the flag stays false but does NOT assert the queue is unmodified — it leaves official-1 in the queue. This mutation predates FIX4 (the auto-add was always before the switch); FIX4 only moved the DB FLAG write, not the queue write. So FIX4 does not worsen it and is still a net improvement on flag consistency.
findings.impact: After a failed enable, the queue retains a provider that can never be switched to (official), so subsequent enable attempts deterministically fail again with P1=official until the operator manually clears the queue. No security impact; soft UX/state wart, single operator.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening: move the empty-queue auto-add to AFTER a successful switch, or roll back the add on switch failure, so a failed enable leaves BOTH the flag and the queue unmodified (full atomicity). Low priority given the operator-gated threat model.

result.dimension: FIX6 (spawn_background_workers) + FIX9-bootstrap dead-code deletion — src-tauri/examples/server.rs, src-tauri/src/bootstrap.rs (+ FE errors.ts/adapter.ts)
result.summary: FIX6 and FIX9-bootstrap are both verified correct and regression-free firsthand. FIX6's spawn_background_workers is a faithful tauri-free port of the desktop lib.rs startup workers: it spawns two fire-and-forget tokio tasks capturing owned Arc<Database> clones, after run_post_db_bootstrap and before serve() (spawned, not awaited). Both periodic_backup_if_needed() and the four session-usage sync fns are fully headless (local-FS read + DB write only; zero outbound HTTP, no AppHandle/Emitter/runtime_ctx dependency), so the spawn-before-proxy-init ordering is race-free. Panic isolation holds (panic = "unwind" + dropped JoinHandle => a worker panic kills only that task, not the server). The webdav/s3 skip is correctly documented and correct (those need AppHandle for *-sync-status-updated events). The web build compiles (cargo check --no-default-features --features web-server --example server: Finished) and the FIX6 pin test passes. FIX9 deletion of RuntimeMode/migration_marker_path is clean: both had ZERO code consumers at HEAD~1 (RuntimeMode was pure dead code; the deleted migration_marker_path's only arg type Path is still used by 4 other live signatures so the import is not orphaned). No source reference to either remains (the only target/ hit is a stale fingerprint artifact). FE WebAuthError/isWebAuthError were also genuinely dead (no catch-site at HEAD~1) so their removal is not a functional regression. One LOW residual: the pre-existing lib.rs:2 comment still names RuntimeMode (now deleted), making an already-stale comment slightly more inaccurate.

findings.title: FIX6: spawn_background_workers is tauri-free, panic-isolated, and correctly ordered (spawned not awaited, after bootstrap)
findings.evidence: main() calls `spawn_background_workers(app_state.as_ref());` (line 313) immediately after `bootstrap::run_post_db_bootstrap(app_state.as_ref());` (301) and before set_runtime_ctx (346)/proxy init (348)/`axum::serve` (405). The fn itself uses two `tokio::spawn(async move { ... })` blocks capturing OWNED clones `let db_for_backup = state.db.clone();` and `let db_for_session_sync = state.db.clone();` (state.db is `Arc<Database>` per store.rs:7), so no borrowed &state escapes into the 'static tasks. No tauri/AppHandle/Emitter symbols anywhere in the fn. Cargo.toml:164 sets `panic = "unwind"`, so a panic in a spawned task unwinds at the task boundary and the dropped JoinHandle means it cannot abort the server process. `cargo test --no-default-features --features web-server --example server main_spawns_background_workers_after_bootstrap` => `test ... ok`.
findings.impact: Headless server now keeps the SQLite DB backed up (initial + daily) and usage fresh (initial + 60s) without relying on lazy on-request work. Faithful desktop parity (identical PERIODIC_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_SECS=24h / SESSION_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECS=60, identical interval.tick() first-tick-skip semantics, identical per-call `if let Err(e)` logging) confirmed against src/lib.rs:679-766.
findings.recommendation: No action. Fix is correct and regression-free.

findings.title: FIX6: background workers have no proxy/runtime-ctx dependency, so spawning before set_runtime_ctx/global-proxy-init is race-free
findings.evidence: spawn_background_workers (server.rs:313) runs at a point where set_runtime_ctx (346) and global outbound proxy init (348/527) have NOT yet executed, and tokio::spawn returns immediately so the workers' INITIAL run can race those steps. Verified the workers need none of it: grep across all four session_usage* modules for `http_client|reqwest|send_http|runtime_ctx|set_runtime|outbound|get_guarded` returns ZERO matches — every `.get(` is `serde_json::Value::get` (JSONL field access). All four `pub fn sync_*` take only `db: &Database`. `periodic_backup_if_needed` (backup.rs:236) only reads settings, scans <data_dir>/backups on disk, and runs backup/cleanup/rollup/vacuum — no UI, no emitter, no AppHandle. They are pure local-FS readers + DB writers.
findings.impact: No ordering hazard: the workers do not depend on proxy/runtime ctx being initialized first. The shared Arc<Database> internal mutex (lock_conn!) serializes DB access; the data-dir flock (_data_lock) guards against a second PROCESS, not in-process tasks, so no flock race. Daily timer holds only an Arc refcount between ticks (no DB lock held across the 24h sleep).
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.title: FIX6: WebDAV/S3 auto-sync workers correctly excluded (require AppHandle); skip is accurately documented

findings.title: FIX9-FE: WebAuthError/isWebAuthError removal is not a functional regression (was dead at HEAD~1); 401 fall-through rationale is sound for Basic-auth single-operator model
findings.evidence: At 072d3d68, `git grep WebAuthError|isWebAuthError -- src/` shows it was only THROWN (`throw new WebAuthError(401, "Session expired")`) and re-exported — there was NO `catch`/`isWebAuthError(e)` consumer, no login-redirect logic. `isWebAuthError` had zero call sites. At HEAD the grep returns nothing (exit 1). The replacement comment: "A 401 from the Basic-Auth-gated `/api` is handled natively by the browser ... a stale/forbidden 401 just falls through to the generic error path below." The 401 branch removal lets it hit the existing `if (!resp.ok)` WebApiError path that callers already handle identically.
findings.impact: Behavioral change (401 now produces a generic WebApiError instead of a never-distinguished WebAuthError) but since nothing ever branched on the typed error, observable behavior is unchanged. Acceptable for the single-operator Basic-auth threat model.
findings.recommendation: No action. (Minor nit: the rationale comment slightly overstates browser auto-reprompt — fetch()/XHR 401s do not always trigger a credential reprompt the way navigations do — but this is immaterial here because the response simply surfaces as a generic error, which is fine.)

result.dimension: FIX1 enforce_outbound_guard threading correctness across services/provider/{mod,usage}.rs + usage_script.rs and call sites (web_api/handlers/{usage,providers}.rs, commands/provider.rs)
result.summary: FIX1 is correctly and completely threaded. The enforce_outbound_guard bool flows through every layer of the usage chain (ProviderService re-exports -> query_usage / query_usage_with_templates / test_usage_script -> execute_and_format_usage_result -> usage_script::execute_usage_script -> send_http_request) with the correct value at each of the 4 leaf call sites: both web handlers (providers.rs:528, usage.rs:348) pass true; both desktop Tauri commands (commands/provider.rs:144,200) pass false. The codex-flagged no-validate path (web query_provider_usage) now reaches guard_outbound_url on the dialed request.url via the custom-script `_ =>` arm. Guard SSOT (proxy::ip_guard::guard_outbound_url + http_client::get_guarded) is tauri-free and internally consistent (is_blocked_ipv4 vs is_blocked_ip dispatch agree). Both runtimes compile clean (cargo check --features web-server AND default desktop). Both new FIX1 unit tests pass (reject 169.254/127.0.0.1/10.x/100.64 CGNAT/file://). Desktop dialing behavior is unchanged (false => identical get() + no-guard path as pre-FIX1). No stale-arity callers in tests/examples. One out-of-scope defense-in-depth residual noted: the native-template arms (TOKEN_PLAN/BALANCE) dial provider-controlled base_url without a pre-dial guard_outbound_url call (they rely only on get_guarded() redirect re-checking) — pre-existing, not introduced by FIX1, and not part of FIX1's claimed custom-script scope.

findings.title: FIX1 enforce_outbound_guard threaded correctly through every layer with correct leaf values (web=true, desktop=false)
findings.lines: usage.rs:507,574,557,681,699,797; mod.rs:2649,2662,2690,2704; usage_script.rs:143,253,377; providers.rs:528; usage.rs(handler):348; provider.rs:144,200
findings.evidence: Every signature in the chain carries the param and forwards it: query_usage(...,enforce_outbound_guard) -> execute_and_format_usage_result(...,enforce_outbound_guard) at usage.rs:557; query_usage_with_templates `_ => query_usage(state, app_type, provider_id, enforce_outbound_guard).await` at usage.rs:681; test_usage_script -> execute_and_format_usage_result(...,enforce_outbound_guard) at usage.rs:797; execute_and_format_usage_result -> `usage_script::execute_usage_script(...,enforce_outbound_guard)` at usage.rs:44/53; execute_usage_script -> `send_http_request(&request, timeout_secs, enforce_outbound_guard)` at usage_script.rs:253. Leaf call sites: providers.rs:528 `Some(state.copilot_auth.as_ref()), // Web runtime ... true,`; usage.rs:348 web handler passes `true`; commands/provider.rs:144 & :200 each pass `// Desktop runtime ... false,`. grep confirms these are the ONLY 4 non-internal callers repo-wide; no other caller passes a wrong value.
findings.impact: The web-only SSRF gate is enabled on exactly the two web entry points and disabled on exactly the two desktop entry points. No layer drops or defaults the flag; no web path defaults to false and no desktop path is forced true.
findings.recommendation: No action. Threading is complete and correct.

findings.title: Codex-flagged no-validate path (web query_provider_usage) now reaches the guard on the dialed request.url
findings.evidence: Web query_provider_usage calls query_usage_with_templates(..., true) at providers.rs:523-531. For a saved custom script (empty/non-native template_type) it falls to the `_ =>` arm (usage.rs:681) which calls query_usage(..., true) -> execute_and_format_usage_result(..., true) -> execute_usage_script(..., true) -> send_http_request(..., true). send_http_request then runs `if enforce_outbound_guard { crate::proxy::ip_guard::guard_outbound_url(&config.url).await.map_err(map_outbound_guard_error)?; }` BEFORE dialing and uses `get_guarded()` for redirect re-checks (usage_script.rs:236-262). guard_outbound_url validates scheme (http/https only) + resolves domain + blocks internal/private/loopback/CGNAT IPs (ip_guard.rs:164-218).
findings.impact: The previously-unvalidated custom-script request.url SSRF vector on the web runtime is closed; the actually-dialed URL (not just the provider base_url) is validated and redirects are re-checked per hop.
findings.recommendation: No action. The flagged path is closed.

findings.title: Desktop dialing behavior unchanged by the signature change (enforce=false => identical pre-FIX1 path); both runtimes compile clean and the two new guard unit tests pass
findings.evidence: send_http_request gates everything on the flag: `let client = if enforce_outbound_guard { get_guarded() } else { get() };` and the guard_outbound_url call is inside `if enforce_outbound_guard`. With false (desktop), the client and skip-guard behavior are byte-identical to pre-FIX1. `cargo check` passed for BOTH `--no-default-features --features web-server` and default desktop (no errors). `cargo test --lib usage_script::tests` (desktop) = 7 passed/0 failed including web_guard_rejects_internal_request_url_before_dial (rejects 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.1, 100.64.0.1) and web_guard_rejects_non_http_scheme (rejects file:///etc/passwd). No stale-arity callers exist in src-tauri/tests or src-tauri/examples for the chain.
findings.impact: No desktop regression; the only desktop delta is an added arg that is ignored when false. No non-usage caller is affected (grep confirmed the only callers of the chain are the usage entry points). The dead ProviderService::query_usage re-export wrapper (mod.rs:2645) has zero external callers and is harmless.
findings.recommendation: No action. (Note: the cc_switch_lib integration-test compile errors under the web-server feature are pre-existing dual-runtime test-gating breakage, unrelated to FIX1 — the lib itself compiles and the lib unit tests pass under desktop.)

findings.title: Native-template usage arms (TOKEN_PLAN/BALANCE) dial provider-controlled base_url without a pre-dial guard_outbound_url call (rely only on get_guarded redirect policy)
findings.evidence: In query_usage_with_templates, the TOKEN_PLAN arm calls `crate::services::coding_plan::get_coding_plan_quota(&credentials.base_url, &credentials.api_key)` and the BALANCE arm calls `crate::services::balance::get_balance(&credentials.base_url, ...)` — neither receives nor consults enforce_outbound_guard. coding_plan.rs and balance.rs do use http_client::get_guarded() internally (verified at coding_plan.rs:92 etc and balance.rs:69 etc), so 30x redirects to internal IPs are blocked, but the INITIAL provider-controlled base_url is never passed through guard_outbound_url, so the first-hop dial to an internal host is not pre-validated. OFFICIAL_SUBSCRIPTION is safe (hardcoded api.anthropic.com/chatgpt.com/googleapis.com via plain get()).
findings.impact: On the web runtime, a provider whose base_url points at an internal host can still be dialed on the first hop for token-plan/balance native templates (an authenticated operator-gated config-write -> SSRF). Low under the single-operator, /api/*-auth-gated threat model. Out of FIX1's claimed scope (FIX1 targeted the custom-script request.url), and pre-existing (not introduced by this commit).
findings.recommendation: For defense-in-depth, thread enforce_outbound_guard into the TOKEN_PLAN/BALANCE arms and call ip_guard::guard_outbound_url(&credentials.base_url) before get_coding_plan_quota/get_balance on the web path (matching the custom-script arm). Optional given operator-gating; track as low/info.

result.dimension: FIX9-frontend (WebAuthError/isWebAuthError removal) + spec accuracy across src/lib/api/adapter.ts, src/lib/api/errors.ts, .trellis/spec/frontend/quality-guidelines.md
result.summary: FIX9 frontend deletion is clean and regression-free: no dangling references to WebAuthError/isWebAuthError/AUTH_ERROR anywhere in src/ (grep empty), credentials:"include" preserved on both mutating fetch paths, and all three FE gates (pnpm typecheck, format:check, check:web-routes missing:0) pass green firsthand. The dropped 401 WebAuthError throw is a benign behavioral change: no consumer ever caught isWebAuthError to drive a re-login UX, so a 401 now harmlessly falls through to the generic WebApiError path (browser handles Basic 401 natively). The Rust half of FIX9 (RuntimeMode/migration_marker_path) is also gone from live source (only a stale doc comment in lib.rs:2 and stale target/ build-cache warnings remain — both cosmetic). Spec FIX1-FIX8 contracts/signatures verified accurate against real code. One spec completeness gap: the +135-line scenario documents FIX1-8 but never mentions the FIX9 frontend deletion, and its "F9 atomicity" label denotes FIX4 (a confusing FIX9-vs-feature-F9 naming collision). Overall: FIX9 correctly closes what it claims with zero regressions.

findings.title: Dropped 401 throw: no re-login UX consumer existed, generic-error fallthrough is acceptable
findings.evidence: Old code threw `new WebAuthError(401, 'Session expired')` before the !resp.ok block. Now a comment replaces it and a 401 falls through to `throw new WebApiError(resp.status, code, errBody.message, errBody.details)` (line 277, code='HTTP_401'). grep across src/**/*.{ts,tsx} for any catch of isWebAuthError / instanceof WebAuthError / .code==='AUTH_ERROR' to drive re-login = zero hits (only the now-deleted definition + throw site ever referenced it). Both fetch sites still attach creds: httpInvoke line 226 `credentials: "include"` and webFetch line 246 `credentials: "include"` — cleanup did NOT drop credentials, so FIX5/Basic-auth still get creds attached.
findings.impact: Non-browser/XHR callers that hit a stale 401 now receive a generic WebApiError(401,'HTTP_401') instead of a typed WebAuthError. Since no code branched on the typed error and the browser re-prompts for Basic creds natively before the response reaches JS, behavior is functionally equivalent for the single-operator browser threat model.
findings.recommendation: No action required. (Defense-in-depth nicety for a hypothetical future multi-user/token-auth mode: a typed 401 would be reintroduced then — but out of scope now.)

findings.title: Spec scenario omits FIX9 and overloads 'F9' to mean FIX4
findings.evidence: The +135-line scenario title and Contracts section document FIX1 through FIX8 explicitly, but there is NO contract, validation row, or test entry for FIX9 (the WebAuthError/isWebAuthError + dead bootstrap RuntimeMode/migration_marker_path removal) — `grep 'FIX 9|FIX9|WebAuthError|RuntimeMode|migration_marker'` in the spec returns nothing. Separately, line 1517 reads '**F9 atomicity (FIX 4)**' where 'F9' is the pre-existing failover feature ID (defined at line 1395 '**F9 (failover-enable SSOT...)**'), colliding with this review round's 'FIX9' label. A future implementer scanning for 'FIX9' or 'F9' could conflate the failover-atomicity fix with the unrelated dead-code cleanup.
findings.impact: Documentation-only. The removed frontend symbols were dead code, so an undocumented deletion creates no runtime risk; but the spec is the contract SSOT and a future maintainer who re-adds WebAuthError-style auth handling has no recorded rationale for why it was removed, and the F9/FIX9 overload is mildly misleading.
findings.recommendation: Add a short FIX9 note to the scenario Contracts ('dead-code cleanup: FE WebAuthError/isWebAuthError removed because Basic-401 is browser-native; Rust bootstrap RuntimeMode/migration_marker_path removed as unused') and either rename the in-scenario 'FIX 4 / F9' references to just 'FIX 4 (failover atomicity)' to avoid the FIX9 collision.
